prompt:
Research the officially documented limits of Cloudflare Workers on the free plan (requests per day, CPU time per request). Cite Cloudflare's own documentation and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
I will research the officially documented limits for Cloudflare Workers on the free plan, specifically focusing on requests per day and CPU time per request.

Here is what I found from Cloudflare's documentation:

SOURCE: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/ | QUOTE: "The Workers Free plan includes 100,000 requests per day." | CLAIM: The free plan for Cloudflare Workers allows 100,000 requests per day.
SOURCE: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/ | QUOTE: "CPU time is the amount of time the CPU is actively processing instructions for your Worker." | CLAIM: Cloudflare defines CPU time separately from wall-clock time.
SOURCE: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/ | QUOTE: "The Free plan has a CPU time limit of 10 ms per request." | CLAIM: The free plan limits CPU time to 10 milliseconds per request.

I was unable to find a source for a specific "requests per day" limit beyond the general 100,000 requests per day, as that is the primary documented limit. There are no additional daily request sub-limits mentioned in the documentation I reviewed. Similarly, for CPU time, 10 ms per request is the only officially documented limit for the free plan.
